pages.text:
ON Semiconductor expects 12% to 14% revenue CAGR through 2030
Onsemi raised its long-term growth targets as AI data center power demand becomes the company's fastest-growing business line
ON Semiconductor just told Wall Street it plans to grow faster than it previously promised. At its Investor/Analyst Day on September 16, 2026, the company raised its long-term revenue growth target to a 12%-14% compound annual rate through 2030.
The old range was 10%-12%.
Under the revised model, onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) is aiming for approximately $11 billion in total revenue by 2030.
The headline act is the company’s AI data center business. Onsemi projects that segment’s revenue will exceed $500 million in 2026 and surpass $2.5 billion by 2030.
That works out to a CAGR of over 50%. The company says that pace would substantially outrun growth in the broader AI data center market.
Onsemi forecasts that semiconductor content per AI rack will climb from about $15,000 today to more than $115,000 by 2030, driven by the industry’s shift toward higher-voltage architectures.

ON Could Be One of the Semiconductor Sector’s Biggest Comeback Stories
ON Semiconductor crashed hard in 2025, but the numbers coming out of its latest quarter tell a very different story, and the question now is whether the market has fully caught on yet.
Published October 13, 2026, 1:30pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
The glowing core of a microchip symbolizes the immense processing power and surging AI demand currently fueling record revenues for semiconductor giants like AMD and Nvidia. © 24/7 Wall St.
The 24/7 Wall St. price target for ON Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) is $96.51 over the next 12 months. From a recent price of $77.53, that works out to 24.48% upside. The stock gets a buy rating from our model, and its confidence is high.
Price Target from 24/7 Wall St.
ON has climbed out of the trough. Revenue fell 22.39% year over year in Q1 2025, then grew 9.18% in Q2 2026. Management now expects AI data center revenue to more than double in 2026, and Q3 guidance calls for non-GAAP EPS of $0.81-$0.93.
A 42% Rally Interrupted by a Sharp Pullback
The stock is up 42.27% year to date and 54.17% over the past year. Over the past week it fell 9.25%, though it is still up 8.54% over the past month. Shares sit well below the 52-week high of $134.92 and well above the low of $44.56.
In Q2, revenue came in at $1.6035B, beating estimates by 0.89%. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.74 against a $0.7153 estimate. Free cash flow reached $425.4M. ON also put through a price adjustment that took effect on October 10, which points to firm demand.
Management raised its 2030 AI data center addressable market from $12 billion to almost $50 billion. All of that expansion still has to be powered, cooled, and connected by somebody, and we rounded up seven of those suppliers in a free AI infrastructure report. Lead times extended from approximately 27 weeks to approximately 32 weeks.
Utilization rose to 83%, and each additional point adds 25 to 30 basis points of gross margin. A $6B buyback adds further support. Among analysts, 2 rate the stock a strong buy and 12 rate it a buy. Our bull case reaches $120.73.
Barclays started coverage at equal-weight with a $75 target and noted ON’s automotive and China exposure. Analog and Mixed-Signal revenue fell 2%. The Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) deal, expected to close in mid-2027, brings integration risk, and the convertible notes could dilute shareholders.
The trailing P/E of 249 looks alarming, but it reflects low 2025 earnings, including $666.9M of restructuring charges. Those charges dropped to $41.2M in Q2. The bear case sits at $79.59.
ON Trades Between NXP and Texas Instruments
NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) is ON’s most direct automotive and industrial rival. It trades at 13x forward earnings while growing revenue 19.48%, so ON looks pricier on recovery-stage earnings.
Texas Instruments (NASDAQ:TXN) is the analog and power benchmark. It commands 28x forward earnings on 22.82% growth. Our target implies about 24x forward EPS, which sits between the two. That looks reasonable as long as ON’s margins keep recovering.
ON Semiconductor Price Prediction 2026-2030
I see the 24/7 Wall St. price target of $96.51 as well supported, and our model’s buy rating carries 90% confidence. Operating leverage is the key factor.
The thesis gets stronger if Q3 gross margin lands within the 40%-42% guidance. It weakens if automotive demand fades or the Synaptics integration struggles. I think the recovery has further to run.
Going forward, here is where our model projects ON could trade, assuming current growth trends and market conditions hold.

These projections assume ON keeps executing its current strategy. The adoption of 800-volt data center architectures could push results higher, while a decline in automotive demand could pull them lower.

pages.title: Jim Cramer isn't giving up on semiconductor stocks despite the sell off. Here's why
pages.text:
Jim Cramer on semiconductor stocks after six-day sell off
CNBC’s Jim Cramer said investors shouldn't give up on semiconductor stocks despite the recent sell-off, arguing that strong demand for chips continues to support the industry's long-term growth.
Cramer highlighted Micron's long-term customer agreements and the expanding use of CPUs from Intel and AMD as reasons the sector's underlying fundamentals remain strong.
The memory group has been the most beaten up and discouraging, says Jim Cramer
Semiconductor stocks have been getting crushed in recent days, but CNBC's Jim Cramer said Tuesday there's a compelling reason not to give up on the group.
The VanEck Semiconductor ETF has fallen 7.2% over six consecutive sessions, and Cramer warned that rising oil prices and interest rates could prolong the sell off. However, he argued chip stocks are increasingly trading together regardless of their individual fundamentals, obscuring the strong demand that fueled the sector's remarkable rally earlier this year.
To illustrate his point, Cramer described a recent visit to an Apple showroom, where he saw devices featuring a more personalized Siri and advanced smart home technology. The experience highlighted how increasingly sophisticated consumer products require more computing power and memory, creating additional opportunities for chipmakers.
"Before you decide to bail from the semis because you can't take the pain, go to the showroom," the "Mad Money" host said. "Go see where these chips are used. They appear in places that you'd least expect them. Don't watch the semiconductor index, watch the devices."
Cramer pointed to memory chip maker Micron as an example of a company whose fundamentals are being overshadowed by the broader sell off. The company has become one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence build-out, with demand for memory chips far outstripping supply. Cramer highlighted its 26 long-term customer agreements, which currently cover about 35% of revenue through 2030, with negotiations already underway for 2031. Those take-or-pay contracts require customers to honor their financial commitments, he said, giving Micron greater visibility into future revenue. "If Micron had no agreements I would be worried," Cramer said.
And the demand story isn't limited to memory chips. Cramer also highlighted Intel and AMD, which "make the CPUs that are basic building blocks for practically every machine under the sun."
Cramer acknowledged that the group could face further losses after its enormous run, but said investors shouldn't dismiss the fundamental demand behind those gains. "It's reasonable to expect a sharp pullback after how far these stocks traveled," he said. "I just think that when you see the devices, when you know the exploding use cases, you can understand why Micron or Intel or AMD have been moving up."
"It wasn't all Situational Awareness, the wayward hedge fund that took so many semis up to unsustainable levels with borrowed money," Cramer said. "A lot of this is just raw demand."

On Semiconductor Climbs 8%, Synaptics Surges 14% as $5.7B Cash Bid Replaces $7B Stock Deal
On Semiconductor scrapped its stock deal for Synaptics and replaced it with cash, and both stocks surged on the news for reasons that point in opposite directions.
Published October 2, 2026, 9:13am ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
A revised takeover agreement is lifting both the buyer and the target in a chip deal that just got simpler. On Semiconductor (NASDAQ:ON | ON Price Prediction) stock is at $86.64, up 8% in morning trading. This follows the company replacing its $7 billion all-stock agreement to buy Synaptics (NASDAQ:SYNA) with a $5.7 billion all-cash bid.
Synaptics stock is up 14% to $121.32, a larger climb tied to a fixed cash price replacing a floating share exchange.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) is up 3% to $590.75, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) trades at $752.16, up 1.36%. That gap shows how much of the move traces to the deal itself.
Under an amended merger agreement, On Semiconductor will pay $123 in cash for each Synaptics share, replacing the all-stock structure. The amendment followed an unsolicited competing proposal for Synaptics from a third party.
On Semiconductor now expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to adjusted earnings per share upon closing. CEO Hassane El-Khoury stated: “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration.” Funding comes from cash on hand and committed debt financing, with no closing condition tied to that financing.
Dilution Fades for On Semiconductor, Certainty Arrives for Synaptics
For On Semiconductor shareholders, the core change is the removal of dilution. Paying cash leaves the share count untouched, protecting buyback work that included $332 million of repurchases in Q2 2026.
A fixed cash price gives Synaptics investors certainty, and the Synaptics board unanimously backed the amended transaction.
Synaptics also brings growth. Its management expects fiscal 2026 Core Internet of Things (IoT) revenue to grow more than 40% to over $385 million, driven by Edge AI and Physical AI design wins. On Semiconductor management stated on the August 3 earnings call that Synaptics’ “market-leading connected compute capabilities” complement On Semiconductor’s “strength in power, sensing, and control.”
The trade-off is debt. Cash and short-term investments totaled $3.9 billion at the end of Q2, with total liquidity of $5.4 billion. Quarterly free cash flow reached $425 million, a support for paying down new borrowing.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the deal, but other jurisdictions are still reviewing it, and Synaptics shareholders must vote. On August 3, On Semiconductor expected the transaction to close in mid-2027.
Investors can watch for the Synaptics stockholder vote and remaining reviews in other jurisdictions before On Semiconductor closes the purchase, as details on the committed debt financing cost could shape how the market judges On Semiconductor’s balance sheet.
Immediate accretion and an AI data center business where management expects revenue to more than double in 2026 support the optimistic view (we covered seven suppliers riding that same AI infrastructure expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report). Risks center on new leverage and integrating Synaptics.
Synaptics shareholders now face an outcome fixed at the $123 cash price. Traders may watch whether On Semiconductor stock holds its gains as borrowing terms become clearer.

Advanced EliteSiC hybrid technology maximizes usable energy as electricity demand surges
As AI-driven electricity demand accelerates worldwide, utilities and energy providers are under growing pressure to store and deliver energy more efficiently. Battery energy storage system (BESS) providers are seeking advanced power conversion technologies to improve performance and system economics. To address these needs, Sungrow has adopted onsemi's latest SiC hybrid power module technology for its PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The design improves system efficiency, helping utilities and energy providers increase usable energy output while lowering operating costs.
onsemi's EliteSiC hybrid power module enables the highest-density battery energy storage system deployments, helping energy providers meet growing electricity demand from AI, renewable energy and electrification
New BESS architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, helping maximize energy delivered to the grid while reducing losses and improving reliability
Sungrow's PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform integrates onsemi's latest EliteSiC hybrid power module technology, optimized for high-power DC-AC energy conversion in utility-scale battery storage applications
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) today announced that Sungrow, a global leader in renewable energy technology, has adopted onsemi's latest EliteSiC silicon carbide (SiC) hybrid power module technology for the Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 energy storage platform. The integration enables improved efficiency and enhanced system performance for utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS).
Helping Sungrow Deliver More Usable Energy
The PowerTitan 3.0 platform incorporates onsemi's high-density power integrated modules (PIMs), optimized for advanced three-level inverter architectures used in high-power energy storage applications.
Compared with the previous-generation platform, the new architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, enabling higher-power battery storage deployments without sacrificing efficiency. The architecture supports power conversion units rated up to 450 kW, contributing to the platform's increased power density and higher-power deployment capability.
With the performance advantages of SiC, the solution supports key system-level benefits including:
Peak efficiency exceeding 99.3% to reduce energy loss in utility-scale systems
Increased power density supports higher-power BESS deployments
Enhanced thermal performance supports reliable operation in high-power applications
Improved system economics through a hybrid SiC design optimized for large-scale deployment
The design win builds on a long-standing strategic relationship between onsemi and Sungrow. Through extensive engineering and validation activities, the companies collaborated throughout platform definition, system optimization and qualification to meet the demanding performance requirements of next-generation energy storage deployments.
"PowerTitan 3.0 represents Sungrow's continued innovation in advanced energy storage system design," said Chen Peng, General Manager of Energy Storage Conversion Product Line at Sungrow Energy Storage Business Unit. "By integrating advanced technologies and collaborating with strategic partners such as onsemi, Sungrow is accelerating the deployment of higher-performance storage solutions that deliver greater value throughout the lifecycle of energy assets. With growing market recognition, Sungrow estimates delivering 10 GWh of PowerTitan 3.0 across Europe in 2026, further supporting the region's transition toward a more flexible and resilient energy system."
"At utility scale, even small improvements in power conversion efficiency can have a meaningful impact on battery energy storage system (BESS) performance and total cost of ownership," said Sergio Fissore, Vice President and General Manager, IPD Power Division, onsemi. "Our EliteSiC hybrid power module enables higher-efficiency, higher-density energy storage systems that help maximize usable energy and improve system reliability. Together with Sungrow, we're advancing the power conversion technologies needed to support the next generation of energy infrastructure."
At utility scale, even small efficiency improvements can generate meaningful financial and environmental benefits. According to onsemi analysis, a 0.4% efficiency improvement delivered by the new SiC hybrid module could save more than 475 MWh of energy annually in a 100 MW battery energy storage installation compared with the previous-generation module.
Those energy savings can help reduce operating costs, increase usable energy delivered to customers and lower overall emissions. The architecture also enables higher overload capability and improved thermal performance, helping customers extract more usable energy from every storage asset.
Supporting the Infrastructure Behind the AI Era
Utilities and energy providers are seeking ways to store more energy, reduce conversion losses and improve overall system economics to meet unprecedented demand amid the AI infrastructure buildout and electrification transition.
Industry forecasts project the battery energy storage market will more than double by 2030 as utilities invest in infrastructure needed to support increasing electricity demand and renewable energy deployment. At the same time, energy storage providers are moving toward higher-power, higher-voltage architectures to improve system economics.

The PowerTitan 3.0 platform incorporates onsemi's high-density power integrated modules (PIMs), optimized for advanced three-level inverter architectures used in high-power energy storage applications.
Compared with the previous-generation platform, the new architecture improves inverter-level efficiency by 0.4%, enabling higher-power battery storage deployments without sacrificing efficiency. The architecture supports power conversion units rated up to 450 kW, contributing to the platform's increased power density and higher-power deployment capability.
With the performance advantages of SiC, the solution supports key system-level benefits including:
Peak efficiency exceeding 99.3% to reduce energy loss in utility-scale systems
Increased power density supports higher-power BESS deployments
Enhanced thermal performance supports reliable operation in high-power applications
Improved system economics through a hybrid SiC design optimized for large-scale deployment

onsemi and Synaptics Announce Revised Merger Agreement
Revised Terms to Deliver Higher onsemi Shareholder Value through Immediate EPS Accretion
Amended Agreement Follows Thorough Review of Unsolicited Competing Proposal
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. and SAN JOSE, Calif. – Oct. 1, 2026 – onsemi (NASDAQ: ON) and Synaptics Incorporated (NASDAQ: SYNA) ("Synaptics") today announced they have amended
their June 25, 2026 merger agreement. The amendment follows an unsolicited competing proposal received from a third party.
Under the revised agreement, onsemi will acquire Synaptics for $123 per share in cash for an aggregate value of approximately $5.7 billion as compared to approximately $7
billion for the prior agreement. The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to onsemi’s non-GAAP earnings per share and provides value certainty for Synaptics’ shareholders.
“As was the case when we initially announced the acquisition, Synaptics addresses an important aspect of our strategic direction, and we believe the revised merger
agreement represents a more financially attractive transaction for our shareholders,” said Hassane El-Khoury, President and CEO of onsemi. “The all-cash transaction delivers higher value to our shareholders through lower total cost consideration,
and we now expect the transaction to be immediately accretive to non-GAAP EPS upon closing. In addition, we have identified incremental opportunities to create shareholder value beyond the previously announced $200 million of annual run-rate
synergies. These additional benefits from revenue synergies and insourcing of a portion of Synaptics’ production are expected to be realized after the initial 18 months
post-close, further strengthening the long-term earnings and cash flow profile of the combined company.”
El-Khoury continued, “Synaptics is accretive to our long-term model, with a strong growth outlook and attractive gross margin profile that will help accelerate onsemi’s
evolution. Additionally, Synaptics complements growth in our AI data center business, and brings to onsemi its highly profitable human-machine interface, and sensing products businesses that generate strong and predictable cash flows, providing the
combined company with a durable funding engine to accelerate its connected compute capabilities.”
After careful review with its financial and legal advisors, the Synaptics Board unanimously determined that the onsemi transaction, as amended, continues to be in the
best interests of Synaptics and its shareholders.
"Our Board has been singularly focused on delivering the best outcome for our shareholders, and today's amended agreement reflects that commitment," said Rahul Patel,
Synaptics President and CEO. “By transitioning to an all-cash structure, we are providing value certainty at a meaningful premium as compared to current value. We are confident this path is the right choice for our shareholders."
The transaction will be financed through a combination of cash on hand and committed financing. onsemi has obtained fully committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley.
The amended merger agreement does not include a closing condition related to onsemi’s financing.
The transaction is still expected to close by mid-2027, subject to approval by Synaptics shareholders, the receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary
closing conditions. The transaction has been approved by the United States Federal Trade Commission, and regulators in other jurisdictions are reviewing the transaction.
